headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surfaces can feed PaddleOCR document outputs into downstream parsing, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct shared-workspace evidence raises uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, events, and webhooks, so its outputs can be consumed as structured input. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers with allowlisted egress, so if OpenMetadata content is routed into OCR or browser-fed text, instruction-like payloads could be misread. No direct shared-channel evidence exists, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are forwarded into PaddleOCR prompts or browser-visible text without sanitization, injection risk materializes.
IF a shared MCP or API bridge passes raw content between the agents, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Sanitize and strip instructions from OpenMetadata outputs before passing them onward.
Disable browser-based ingestion for untrusted content paths.
Add a fixed schema/allowlist for fields PaddleOCR may consume.
Insert a human review step for any content that originated outside the pair.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end so downstream parsers can reject untrusted instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data classes, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or uncontrolled third-party upload path between them. Leakage is therefore plausible only through operator-mediated transfer or an undocumented bridge, making the blast radius limited and the severity low.
conditions: IF the operator copies OpenMetadata exports into PaddleOCR inputs, those data classes can be exposed.
IF a shared workspace is introduced later, document contents may inherit metadata from OpenMetadata outputs.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid sending OpenMetadata exports containing governance or lineage data into OCR jobs.
Redact sensitive fields before any manual transfer.
Review upload destinations for PaddleOCR before processing documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and uses APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser execution. The profiles do not show both writing the same filesystem, git state, or database, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable resource, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend or directory, concurrent updates can collide.
IF an orchestrator grants both write access to one resource, last-writer-wins errors become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories or databases.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Turn off concurrent runs when touching the same artifact.
Check for lock files or transaction support before batch jobs.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking for shared mutable targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit metadata, lineage, and governance facts that PaddleOCR could ingest as document text or browser content. PaddleOCR is not documented as verifying upstream claims, so if its outputs are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or workflows. The interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as authoritative input to another workflow without verification, upstream mistakes can propagate.
IF OpenMetadata-generated facts are rendered into documents that PaddleOCR later extracts, errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require a verification step before downstream use of PaddleOCR output.
Compare extracted fields against source documents or metadata.
Flag low-confidence OCR results for manual review.
Limit automated actions triggered by extracted text.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance and lineage data, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. The profiles do not show residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so no concrete compliance breach is evidenced. A low severity is warranted because compliance issues could arise only if regulated documents are routed from OpenMetadata into PaddleOCR without policy checks.
conditions: IF regulated documents or governed metadata are sent from OpenMetadata to PaddleOCR, policy review is required.
IF retention or deletion policies differ in the surrounding deployment, compliance drift can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before transfer between agents.
Block regulated records from OCR unless approved.
Document retention and deletion handling for both systems.
Review residency and vendor policy for any hosted deployment.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for sensitive documents.
